scenario: 题目是资源分配或区间调度，优化目标明确，物品有一个很自然的排序键（比如结束时间、大小）。
scenario_en: The problem is resource allocation or interval scheduling, has a clear optimization goal, and has a natural sort key such as end time or size.
q: 面对这种天然带排序键的优化题，你该怎么对待贪心？
q_en: How should you treat greedy when an optimization problem has a natural sort key?
options: 先把贪心当候选方案，验证局部选择是否安全
不做验证，直接提交任意排序方案
断定这类题目永远不能用贪心
改把它当字符串解析题来处理
options_en: Treat greedy as a candidate and verify the local choice is actually safe.
Submit any sorted-order solution without verifying it.
Decide this kind of problem can never use greedy.
Treat it as a string-parsing problem instead.
why: 贪心的机会很多，但正确性是有条件的；AI 很容易写出看起来合理的贪心代码。
why_en: Treat greedy as a candidate strategy that still needs justification, not an automatic answer.
whenOtherWins: 如果局部选择会锁死后续组合，或者问题其实是 NP-hard 装箱，贪心可能只是启发式，需要 DP 或回溯兜底。
tradeoff: 贪心跑得快、代码简单 vs 正确性需要先证明或反例验证
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Greedy idea] --> B{Can prove local choice?}
B -->|yes| C[Use greedy]
B -->|no| D[Look for DP or search]
C --> E[Test counterexamples]

termDefinitions.meaning: 每一步都做当前看起来最优的选择、且不回头调整的算法策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step and never reconsiders it.

optionExplanations: 候选而非结论：排序键给了贪心机会，但仍要靠交换论证或反例把它坐实。
跳过验证等于把'看起来对'当成'证明对'，反例往往几秒就能戳穿这类方案。
一刀切拒绝贪心会错过区间调度这类确实有精确贪心解的题目。
排序键指向的是资源分配/调度结构，跟字符串解析没有关系，判错了问题类型。
optionExplanations_en: Greedy earns a look here because of the sort key, but it still needs an exchange argument or counterexample before you trust it.
Skipping verification treats 'looks right' as 'proven right' -- a counterexample can break it in seconds.
Ruling out greedy outright would miss problems like interval scheduling that do have a provably exact greedy solution.
The sort key points to resource allocation or scheduling, not string parsing -- that's the wrong problem category.

q: 哪些信号说明一个优化题值得先考虑贪心？
q_en: Which signals make an optimization problem worth considering greedy first?
options: 优化目标带自然排序键，比如按结束时间、大小或时长排序
当前这步的选择不会严重限制下一步能选什么
题目属于资源分配、调度、区间管理或装箱
题目要求穷举列出所有合法解
options_en: The optimization goal has a natural sort key, like end time, size, or duration.
The choice at this step doesn't badly constrain what you can pick next.
The problem is resource allocation, scheduling, interval management, or bin packing.
The problem asks you to enumerate every valid solution.
why: 前三项说明局部选择可能有全局意义；穷举所有解通常是回溯问题，不是贪心信号。
why_en: Natural ordering, low future coupling, and allocation-or-scheduling domains are the classic greedy cues.
optionExplanations: 排序键让你能一次线性扫描做决策，省去回头比较所有组合的搜索空间。
选择互不牵连，挡住了'现在选的会不会锁死后面'这个最大的贪心风险。
这些领域历史上多有可证明的贪心解法，值得先起草一个基线再验证。
要求列出所有解指向的是回溯/DFS，硬套贪心会漏掉大部分合法解。
optionExplanations_en: A sort key means one linear pass instead of comparing every combination.
Choices that don't constrain the future rule out the biggest greedy risk -- an early pick locking out later options.
These domains have a track record of provable greedy solutions, worth a greedy baseline first.
Needing every valid solution points to backtracking or DFS; forcing greedy here would miss most solutions.

q: 填空：贪心正确的两个核心性质。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: the two core properties that make greedy correct.
text: 贪心要正确，通常需要{{贪心选择性质}}和{{最优子结构}}同时成立。
why: 局部最优选择必须不会破坏全局最优，做完选择后剩下的问题还要像原问题的缩小版。缺一项，贪心就可能只是看起来合理。
why_en: Greedy correctness depends on the greedy-choice property and optimal substructure.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Choice[Greedy choice] --> Safe[Does not hurt optimum]
  Safe --> Sub[Remaining subproblem]
  Sub --> Repeat[Repeat same rule]
  Repeat --> Opt[Global result]

termDefinitions.meaning: 局部最优选择不会妨碍达到全局最优解的性质。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The greedy-choice property means a locally optimal choice never prevents reaching the global optimum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 做完一次选择后，剩下的子问题仍是同类型问题的一个更小实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimal substructure means the remaining subproblem is a smaller instance of the same type of problem.

q: 提交贪心方案前，应该先问自己哪几个诊断问题？
q_en: What diagnostic questions should you ask before submitting a greedy solution?
options: 我能做出一个选择、并且永远不用撤销它吗？
做完一个选择后，剩下的问题还是同类型的小问题吗？
能不能构造一个小反例，让这个策略给出错误答案？
AI 生成代码的速度快，是不是就意味着它一定正确？
options_en: Can I make a choice and never need to undo it?
After one choice, does the remaining problem look like a smaller version of the same thing?
Can I construct a small counterexample where this strategy fails?
Does the AI generating code quickly mean the code must be correct?
why: 这些问题分别检查可提交性、最优子结构和反例。AI 生成速度不等于算法正确。
why_en: Before trusting greedy, ask whether choices can be committed, whether the remaining problem is similar, and whether a counterexample exists.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Before submitting] --> B[State local rule]
B --> C[Try exchange argument]
C --> D[Test small counterexample]
D --> E[Name exact or heuristic]
optionExplanations: 问这句挡住的是'选完又想反悔'的风险，贪心选择一旦不可逆就必须先确认它安全。
问这句是在确认最优子结构成立，不然规则用到一半就会失效。
主动找反例是最快的证伪方式，几秒钟就能戳穿一个看似合理的贪心。
生成速度快只说明 AI 打字快，跟局部选择是否安全无关，是要打破的错误直觉。
optionExplanations_en: This checks whether the choice is truly irreversible -- the biggest risk if you'd ever need to undo it.
This confirms optimal substructure holds, otherwise the rule breaks down partway through.
Hunting for a counterexample is the fastest way to disprove a greedy idea that only looks reasonable.
Fast generation only means the AI types quickly -- it says nothing about whether the choice is safe, and that's the assumption to break.

q: 为什么说贪心是最容易“看起来对但其实错”的模式？
q_en: Why is greedy so likely to look right while being wrong?
options: 贪心代码写出来通常无法通过编译
有诱人的局部选择，但只有部分能保证全局最优
贪心算法只能处理字符串类型的输入
贪心方案的运行速度永远比动态规划慢
options_en: Greedy code usually fails to compile.
There's a tempting local choice, but only some choices are actually globally optimal.
Greedy algorithms only work on string inputs.
Greedy is always slower than dynamic programming.
why: 自然排序会诱导你和 AI 过早提交策略。真正要证明的是这个局部选择不会牺牲未来最优。
why_en: Greedy is risky because many problems have tempting local choices but only some make those choices globally safe.
tradeoff: 看似合理的局部选择 vs 站得住脚的全局最优证明
optionExplanations: 贪心代码语法上通常完全合法、能编译能跑，这正是它危险的地方，不是编译问题。
危险来自看起来合理的局部选择，未必等于全局最优，这正是要每次单独证明的地方。
贪心广泛用在区间、装箱、图论等非字符串问题上，限定成字符串处理是判错了范围。
有些贪心（如区间调度）是精确解且比 DP 快得多，速度比较不能替代正确性判断。
optionExplanations_en: Greedy code is usually syntactically fine and compiles and runs -- that's exactly what makes it dangerous, not a compile error.
The risk is a locally tempting choice that isn't automatically globally optimal -- that's what needs proving each time.
Greedy is widely used for intervals, packing, and graphs, not just strings -- that's the wrong scope.
Some greedy solutions, like interval scheduling, are exact and faster than DP -- speed doesn't decide correctness.

q: 硬币找零中，面额 `[1, 3, 4]`、目标 6 为什么能反驳“每次取最大硬币”？
q_en: In coin change with denominations [1, 3, 4] and target 6, why does this disprove largest-coin-first?
options: 贪心选 6 枚，最优需要 7 枚
这个金额在该面额系统下无解
得到 4+1+1 三枚，最优是 3+3 两枚
取最大硬币策略在任意面额下都最优
options_en: Greedy uses six coins while the optimum needs seven.
This amount has no valid solution under this coin system.
It takes 4+1+1, three coins, while the optimum is 3+3, two coins.
Largest-coin-first is always optimal for any denomination set.
why: 一次看似最好的 4 会把后续逼进两个 1。这个小反例证明贪心选择性质在任意面额下不成立。
why_en: The 1,3,4 coin system breaks largest-coin greedy because 4 plus 1 plus 1 is worse than 3 plus 3.
tradeoff: 贪心选最大面额（简单快）vs 动态规划找到真正最优组合
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Six[Amount 6] --> Four[Take 4]
  Four --> One[Take 1]
  One --> One2[Take 1]
  Six --> ThreeA[Take 3]
  ThreeA --> ThreeB[Take 3]
optionExplanations: 枚数对不上真实计算过程，贪心走的是 4+1+1 三枚，不是六枚。
面额里含 1 就一定有解，这个选项在起点就站不住。
贪心先拿 4 把自己逼进两个 1，比 3+3 多花一枚，这正是反例要证明的落差。
这句话就是被这个反例推翻的断言，反例存在本身已经否定它。
optionExplanations_en: The coin count is wrong -- greedy actually takes 4+1+1, three coins, not six.
A coin set with 1 in it always has a solution, so this option fails at the starting premise.
Greedy grabs 4 first and gets boxed into two 1s, one coin worse than 3+3 -- exactly the gap the counterexample shows.
This is the very claim the counterexample disproves; its existence already refutes the statement.

scenario: 给一组会议区间，目标是选择最多数量的互不重叠会议。
scenario_en: Given meeting intervals, the goal is to choose the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings.
q: 给定这些会议区间，标准的贪心策略应该怎么排序、怎么选？
q_en: For these meeting intervals, how should the standard greedy strategy sort and select?
options: 按开始时间从晚到早排序后再选
按会议名称的字母顺序排序后再选
不排序，直接优先选时长最长的会议
按结束时间排序，依次选最早结束且不冲突的会议
options_en: Sort by start time from latest to earliest.
Sort meetings alphabetically by name.
Skip sorting and always pick the longest meeting first.
Sort by end time and repeatedly pick the earliest-ending compatible meeting.
why: 最早结束的会议给未来留下最多空间。这个问题的交换论证很经典，所以贪心是精确最优而不是启发式。
why_en: Maximum non-overlapping interval scheduling is solved by choosing the earliest-ending compatible interval.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题改成带权收益最大化，单纯最早结束不够，通常需要加 DP。
tradeoff: 按结束时间贪心（可证明精确最优）vs 按开始时间/名称/时长排序（无法保证最优）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Sort[Sort by end time] --> First[Pick earliest end]
  First --> Compatible[Skip conflicts]
  Compatible --> Next[Pick next compatible]
  Next --> Result[Max count]
optionExplanations: 开始时间晚不代表给后面留的空间少，排序方向本身就选错了维度。
名字顺序和会议的时间结构没有任何关系，纯属误用排序键。
只挑时长最长的会议容易占满本可以塞下多场短会的时间段，选出的场数反而更少。
最早结束的会议留给后续的空间最大，这是有交换论证撑腰的标准精确解。
optionExplanations_en: A later start time doesn't mean less room left for later meetings -- this sorts on the wrong dimension entirely.
Alphabetical order has no relationship to the timing structure of the meetings -- it's just the wrong key.
Picking the longest meeting first can hog a slot that could've fit several shorter ones, so the total count drops.
The earliest-ending meeting leaves the most room for what comes after -- the exact solution backed by an exchange argument.

q: 填空：区间调度为什么按结束时间贪心？
q_en: Fill in the blanks: why does interval scheduling greedily sort by end time?
text: 选择{{最早结束}}的可兼容区间，会给后续区间留下{{最多空间}}。
why: 如果某个最优解第一个选的不是最早结束区间，通常可以交换成最早结束区间而不减少可选数量。这就是直觉版交换论证。
why_en: Choosing the earliest finishing compatible interval leaves the most room for future intervals.

scenario: 你在给同事审查一段“最大不重叠区间”的贪心实现，想确认这一行条件到底在保证什么。
scenario_en: You are reviewing a greedy implementation for maximum non-overlapping intervals and want to confirm what this condition guarantees.
q: 这段最大不重叠区间代码中，`start >= last_end` 的含义是什么？
q_en: In this maximum non-overlapping interval code, what does `start >= last_end` mean?
options: 当前区间和上一个已选区间不重叠，可以安全加入
当前区间必须比上一个已选区间更短
当前区间是这批区间里权重最大的
当前区间一定是排序后的最后一个
options_en: The current interval doesn't overlap the last selected one, so it's safe to add.
The current interval must be shorter than the last selected one.
The current interval has the largest weight among all intervals.
The current interval must be the last one after sorting.
why: 排序保证遍历顺序是结束时间递增；这个条件只负责兼容性。选中后更新 last_end，作为后续区间的边界。
why_en: The condition checks compatibility with the last selected interval after sorting by end time.
optionExplanations: start >= last_end 就是不重叠的判定式，满足才 append 并推进 last_end。
代码里根本没有比较区间长度，长度约束是凭空加上去的。
这段代码没有权重字段，也没按权重排序，权重这个概念在这里不存在。
排序只保证遍历顺序按结束时间递增，选中的不一定是数组里位置最后的那个。
optionExplanations_en: `start >= last_end` is literally the no-overlap test -- pass it and the code appends and advances `last_end`.
The code never compares interval lengths, so a length requirement is invented out of nowhere.
There's no weight field or weight-based sort in this snippet -- weight isn't a concept here at all.
Sorting only guarantees traversal order by end time, not that the selected interval sits last in the array.

scenario: 给一组会议区间，目标是需要的最少房间数，而不是最多能选多少会议。
scenario_en: Given meeting intervals, the goal is the minimum number of rooms needed, not the maximum number of meetings selected.
q: 面对“最少需要多少房间”这个目标，应该用哪种贪心结构？
q_en: For the goal of minimum rooms needed, which greedy structure should you use?
options: 按结束时间排序，贪心选最多不重叠的区间
按开始时间排序，用最小堆维护当前活跃会议的最早结束时间
忽略时间顺序，每次都优先安排时长最长的会议
用并查集（Union-Find）把重叠的会议合并成一组
options_en: Sort by end time and greedily pick the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals.
Sort by start time and keep a min-heap of the earliest end time among active meetings.
Ignore time order and always schedule the longest meeting first.
Use union-find to merge overlapping meetings into groups.
why: 最少房间数等价于任意时刻最大重叠数。最小堆记录活跃会议的结束时间，能判断是否复用房间。
why_en: Minimum meeting rooms uses a min-heap of active end times after sorting by start time.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是最多选择多少不重叠会议，才使用按结束时间选择的区间调度策略。
tradeoff: 统计任意时刻最大重叠数（最小堆）vs 选出最多不重叠子集（按结束时间贪心）

flowchart TD
  Meeting[Next meeting by start] --> Heap[Min heap of end times]
  Heap --> Reuse{Earliest end <= start?}
  Reuse -->|yes| Pop[Reuse room]
  Reuse -->|no| New[Need new room]
  Pop --> Push[Push current end]
  New --> Push

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种维护不相交集合、支持快速合并和查询的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Union-Find is a data structure that tracks disjoint sets and supports fast merge and lookup operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆顶总是当前最小元素的优先队列结构。

rows: 维护活跃区间最早结束时间
背包式近似（非区间调度标准解）
合并重叠区间为连通分量
分组/连通性问题，不是计数问题

optionExplanations: 这是'选最多不重叠会议数'那题的正确贪心，但这里问的是房间数，目标换了策略也要换。

并查集擅长找连通分量，不维护'谁先结束'这种时间顺序，答不出房间数。

The heap top is the earliest-ending active meeting, so you can instantly tell whether a room can be reused.
Sorting by duration says nothing about how many meetings overlap at any instant, which is what room count tracks.
Union-find groups connected components; it doesn't track who finishes first, so it can't answer a room-count question.

q: 最大不重叠区间和最少会议室为什么不能用同一套贪心？
q_en: Why can't maximum non-overlapping intervals and minimum meeting rooms use the same greedy strategy?
options: 两题的输入区间格式完全不同，没法类比
最少会议室问题的区间不能先排序处理
最大不重叠区间问题必须依赖动态规划求解
前者选最大不重叠子集，后者统计最大重叠数
options_en: The two problems' input interval formats are completely different, so they can't be compared.
The minimum-rooms problem can't be sorted first.
Maximum non-overlapping intervals must rely on dynamic programming.
One selects the maximum non-overlapping subset; the other counts the maximum simultaneous overlap.
why: 两个题都长得像区间题，但目标不同。目标变化会改变贪心选择和数据结构。
why_en: Selecting a maximum compatible subset is different from counting active resources, so the greedy strategy changes.
tradeoff: 选子集最大化数量（排序扫描）vs 统计同时活跃资源数（最小堆）

rows: 最大不重叠区间（按结束时间贪心）
维护活跃区间最早结束时间

optionExplanations: 两题输入其实都是 (start, end) 区间，格式一样，问题不在输入。
两题都要先排序，只是一个按开始、一个按结束，排序本身不是障碍。
最大不重叠区间有 O(n log n) 的贪心精确解，不需要 DP。
一个在选子集、一个在数峰值，目标不同才是排序键和数据结构都要换的根因。
optionExplanations_en: Both problems take the same (start, end) interval format -- the input isn't where they diverge.
Both problems sort first, just on different keys (start vs. end) -- sorting itself isn't the obstacle.
Maximum non-overlapping intervals has an exact O(n log n) greedy solution; it never needed DP.
One selects a subset, the other counts a peak -- that goal difference is why the sort key and structure both change.

scenario: 你在审查一段“最少会议室”贪心实现，想确认堆顶条件到底在判断什么。
scenario_en: You are reviewing a greedy minimum-meeting-rooms implementation and want to confirm what the heap-top condition checks.
q: 这段最少会议室代码中，`heap[0] <= start` 表示什么？
q_en: In this minimum-meeting-rooms code, what does `heap[0] <= start` mean?
options: 当前这个会议必须被丢弃，不能安排
说明所有房间此刻都空闲着
最早结束的会议已经结束，可以复用这个房间
堆里保存的是每个会议的开始时间
options_en: The current meeting must be dropped and can't be scheduled.
It means every room is currently free.
The heap top (earliest-ending active meeting) has already ended, so this room can be reused.
The heap stores each meeting's start time.

why_en: The heap top is the earliest ending active meeting, so it can be reused if it ends before the new start.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a priority queue whose top element is always the current smallest value.

optionExplanations: 代码逻辑里没有丢弃分支，条件成立时走的是复用房间，不是丢弃会议。

A non-empty heap means at least one room is currently occupied, which contradicts 'every room is free.'

scenario: 任务有不同内存需求，服务器容量固定，目标是用尽量少的服务器装下所有任务。
scenario_en: Tasks have different memory needs, server capacity is fixed, and the goal is to fit all tasks using as few servers as possible.
q: 这个“用最少服务器装下所有任务”的问题，更接近下面哪种经典问题？
q_en: This use-the-fewest-servers-to-fit-all-tasks problem is closest to which classic problem?
options: Edit distance：计算把一个字符串变成另一个的最少编辑步数
拓扑排序：给有依赖关系的任务排出一个合法顺序
无权图最短路：找从起点到终点边数最少的路径
Bin packing：把所有物品装进尽量少的固定容量箱子
options_en: Edit distance: compute the minimum edits to turn one string into another.
Topological sort: order dependent tasks into one valid sequence.
Unweighted shortest path: find the path with the fewest edges.
Bin packing: pack all items into as few fixed-capacity bins as possible.
why: 装箱的目标是把所有物品放入尽量少的固定容量箱子。精确最优是 NP-hard，面试里常接受清楚说明的贪心基线。
why_en: Minimizing servers for fixed-capacity tasks is a bin-packing problem where greedy heuristics are often the practical interview answer.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目要求精确最优且规模很小，可考虑回溯/搜索；如果是选子集最大价值，那是 knapsack 而非 bin packing。
tradeoff: 贪心装箱启发式（快、近似）vs 精确最优搜索（慢、NP-hard 才需要）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一批物品装进容量固定的箱子、目标是用最少箱子数的经典问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bin packing is the classic problem of fitting items into fixed-capacity bins using as few bins as possible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需的最少插入/删除/替换次数。

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每条边都从前面指向后面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so every edge points from earlier to later.

optionExplanations: 编辑距离处理字符串变换步数，跟'装得下装不下'的容量约束毫无关系。

Shortest path cares about path length; this problem is about whether things fit, with no start-to-end path concept.
Tasks map to items and server capacity maps to bin capacity -- using the fewest bins to fit everything is exactly bin packing.

q: 文章列出的装箱贪心策略有哪些？
q_en: Which bin-packing greedy strategies are listed here?
options: First-Fit：把物品放进第一个能容纳它的箱子
Best-Fit：把物品放进剩余空间最少但仍能容纳的箱子
First-Fit Decreasing：先按大小降序排序，再做 First-Fit
永远只把最小的物品放进箱子，直到所有箱子都满
options_en: First-Fit: place the item in the first bin that has room.
Best-Fit: place the item in the tightest bin that still fits.
First-Fit Decreasing: sort items largest-first, then apply First-Fit.

why: FFD 先处理大物品，减少后续无法放置的风险。小物品先放容易造成碎片化。
why_en: First-Fit, Best-Fit, and First-Fit Decreasing are the common bin-packing greedy strategies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 扫描已有箱子，把物品放进第一个能装下它的箱子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit scans existing bins and places the item in the first one that has enough room.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把物品放进放入后剩余空间最小、但仍能装下它的箱子。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把物品按大小从大到小排序，再依次执行 First-Fit 装箱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest-first, then applies First-Fit bin packing.

optionExplanations: 扫到第一个能装下就放，实现最简单，代价是容易留下零碎空间。
多扫一遍找最紧的箱子，打包更紧凑，但每次都要多比较。
先按大小降序排再 First-Fit，先处理大物品能显著降低后期无处安放的风险。
只放小物品会让箱子很快被填满、大件却没地方去，装箱数会远多于必要值。
optionExplanations_en: Place into the first bin that fits -- simplest to implement, at the cost of leaving fragmented space behind.
Scan for the tightest-fitting bin -- packs denser, but costs an extra comparison pass each time.
Sort largest-first, then First-Fit -- placing big items early sharply cuts the risk of nowhere to put them later.
Placing only small items fills bins quickly while large ones have nowhere to go, pushing bin count above what's needed.

q: 填空：First-Fit Decreasing 的步骤。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: the steps of First-Fit Decreasing.
text: FFD 先把物品按大小{{降序排序}}，然后对每个物品执行{{First-Fit}}。
why: 先放大物品是一种实用启发式，因为小物品通常更容易塞进剩余空间。它不是保证最优的精确算法。
why_en: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest first and then applies First-Fit.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest-first, then applies First-Fit bin packing.

q_en: What is the rough worst-case bin-count guarantee for FFD?
options: 结果恰好总是等于 OPT 个箱子
无论输入什么，总是需要 2^n 个箱子
目前没有任何已知的近似保证结论

The result is always exactly equal to OPT bins, no matter the input.

why_en: FFD is bounded by about eleven-ninths of the optimal bin count plus six-ninths, which matters for stating it's a bounded heuristic, not an exact optimum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个问题在给定输入下真正的最优解数值，比如最优箱子数。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把物品按大小从大到小排序，再依次执行 First-Fit 装箱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest-first, then applies First-Fit bin packing.

optionExplanations: 这就是 FFD 已知的近似界，说明它是有保证的启发式，不是精确最优算法。
FFD 是近似算法，不保证跟最优箱子数完全相等，这里把近似说成了精确。
2^n 是指数级，装箱问题的箱子数不会随物品数指数爆炸，这个说法夸张失实。
FFD 恰恰是研究得很透的问题，是有明确近似界的，不是没人研究过。
optionExplanations_en: This is FFD's known approximation bound -- it makes FFD a heuristic with a guarantee, not an exact optimum.
FFD is approximate, not guaranteed equal to the optimal bin count -- this mistakes 'bounded' for 'exact.'
Bin count doesn't blow up exponentially with item count the way 2^n implies -- this overstates it wildly.
FFD is actually a well-studied case with a known bound -- this claims no guarantee exists, which is false.

scenario: AI 写了最简单的 FFD：每个物品扫描所有已有箱子。
scenario_en: The AI wrote the simplest FFD implementation: each item scans all existing bins.
q: 这段实现的主要性能特征是什么？
q_en: What is the main performance characteristic of this implementation?
options: 这段代码的时间复杂度恒为 O(1)，与物品数量无关
朴素扫描最坏是 O(n^2)，可用有序结构优化
这段代码保证总能返回精确最优的装箱方案
这段代码完全无法处理任何容量限制条件
options_en: This code's time complexity is constant, O(1), independent of item count.
Naive scanning is O(n^2) in the worst case; an ordered structure can improve it.
This code is guaranteed to always return the exact optimal packing.
This code cannot handle any capacity constraint at all.
why: 每个物品可能扫描所有箱子，所以最坏二次方。除非题目明确要求更快，朴素版在面试中常可作为清晰基线。
why_en: Naive FFD can be quadratic because each item scans existing bins, though ordered capacity tracking can improve it.
whenOtherWins: 如果输入规模大或复杂度要求明确，应该让 AI 用平衡树等结构维护剩余容量。
tradeoff: 朴素双重循环（O(n^2)，实现简单）vs 平衡树/堆维护剩余容量（O(n log n)，实现更复杂）

termDefinitions.meaning: 常数时间复杂度，运行时间基本不随输入规模变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means constant time complexity that does not grow with input size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入规模翻倍时运行时间大约变成四倍的复杂度量级。

optionExplanations: 外层遍历物品、内层遍历箱子，两层循环摆在那，不可能是常数时间。

`load + item <= capacity` 这行本身就在做容量检查，跟'不处理容量'的说法矛盾。

scenario: 服务器同时有 CPU 和内存上限，任务也有两个资源需求。
scenario_en: Each server has both CPU and memory limits, and each task consumes both resources.
q: 服务器同时受 CPU 和内存上限约束时，面试中合理的贪心思路是什么？
q_en: When servers are constrained by both CPU and memory, what is a reasonable greedy interview approach?
options: 只根据任务的名称字符串本身来排序
直接忽略其中一个资源维度的约束
按更紧张的归一化资源需求排序，另一维只作可行性检查
声称一维版本的 FFD 在这里仍然精确最优
options_en: Sort tasks purely by their name string itself.
Simply ignore one of the two resource dimensions.
Sort by the tighter normalized resource demand and use the other dimension only as a feasibility check.
Claim that the one-dimensional version of FFD is still exactly optimal here.
why: 多维装箱更难，实用做法是用一个启发式排序近似处理，并明确说明放弃了精确最优保证。成熟回答会讲清 tradeoff。
why_en: For multi-resource packing, a practical interview heuristic sorts by the tightest normalized resource and checks all capacities.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目要求严格最优且规模很小，可以回溯搜索；如果只需可行分配，启发式更务实。
tradeoff: 归一化排序启发式（务实、放弃精确最优）vs 精确回溯/搜索（能保证最优、规模必须很小）
codeSample:

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同量纲的数值换算到同一个 0 到 1 的比例范围，方便比较。

忽略一个维度会让被忽略的那个资源真的超出服务器上限。
用 max(cpu/cpu_cap, mem/mem_cap) 找出哪个维度更紧张，两个约束都纳入了考虑。
多维装箱比一维更难，一维的精确最优保证不能照搬过来。
optionExplanations_en: The name string has no numerical relationship to CPU or memory usage, so this sort accomplishes nothing.
Ignoring a dimension lets the ignored resource actually blow past the server's real limit.
`max(cpu/cpu_cap, mem/mem_cap)` finds which dimension is tighter, so both constraints get accounted for.
Multi-resource packing is harder than one-dimensional packing; the one-dimensional guarantee doesn't carry over.

q: “贪心近似”和“贪心错误”的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between approximate greedy and wrong greedy?
options: 二者其实完全一样，只是叫法不同，没有区别
近似策略在任何情况下都一定无法返回合法解
错误策略只是运行得慢一点而已，别无其他问题
近似有保证但可能非最优；错误则不满足题意，必须换算法

An approximate strategy can never return any valid solution under any circumstance.
A wrong strategy is merely a bit slower, with no other issue at all.
Approximate can be non-optimal but comes with a stated guarantee; wrong fails the requirement and needs a different algorithm.

why_en: Approximate greedy can be acceptable with stated guarantees, while incorrect greedy fails the required objective.
tradeoff: 近似（非最优但有保证，可接受）vs 错误（不满足题意，必须替换算法）

optionExplanations: 这句话抹掉了两者最关键的区别：是否满足题目要求，二者并不能划等号。

近似能带着已知保证说出口，错误必须承认并换算法，这是两者的真正分界。

A wrong strategy gives the wrong answer outright -- speed was never the issue here.

scenario: 题目是 0/1 knapsack：从物品中选一个子集，在容量内最大化价值。
scenario_en: The problem is 0/1 knapsack: choose a subset of items to maximize value within capacity.
q: 为什么不能直接把它当 bin packing 用 FFD？
q_en: Why can't you directly treat this as bin packing and use FFD?
options: knapsack 选子集要 DP；装箱是尽量少用箱子
这两个问题的容量约束设定完全一样
knapsack 问题里其实没有容量限制
FFD 用在 knapsack 上也总返回最大价值

The knapsack problem actually has no capacity limit.
FFD also always returns the maximum value when used on knapsack.

why_en: Bin packing packs all items into few bins, while zero-one knapsack selects a value-maximizing subset and usually needs DP.
whenOtherWins: 如果是 fractional knapsack，可以按价值密度贪心；0/1 版本不能随意拆分物品。
tradeoff: Bin Packing：装下全部、最少箱子数 vs 0/1 Knapsack：选子集、最大化价值

termDefinitions.meaning: 从若干不可拆分物品中选一个子集，在容量限制内让总价值最大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The 0/1 knapsack problem selects an unsplittable subset of items to maximize total value within a capacity limit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把物品按大小从大到小排序，再依次执行 First-Fit 装箱。

optionExplanations: 一个在选子集最大化价值、一个在装下全部最少化箱子数，目标函数不同，算法自然不同。

scenario: 图最短路问题存在负权边，AI 生成了 Dijkstra。
scenario_en: The shortest-path graph has negative-weight edges, and the AI generated Dijkstra.
q: AI 用 Dijkstra 处理带负权边的最短路，你应该如何纠正？
q_en: If the AI uses Dijkstra on shortest paths with negative edges, how should you correct it?
options: 只把优先队列换成普通队列的实现，其他逻辑完全不变
指出非负权重前提被打破，改用 Bellman-Ford
删掉所有带负权的边，直接回避掉这个问题
断言负权边完全不会影响最短路的最终结果

Point out that the non-negative-weight assumption is broken; switch to Bellman-Ford.
Delete every negative-weight edge outright to sidestep the problem entirely.
Assert that negative edges have no effect on the final shortest-path result at all.
why: Dijkstra 是贪心式扩展最近节点，依赖非负权重。负权会让已确定距离后来变小。

whenOtherWins: 如果确认所有权重非负，Dijkstra 仍然是合适选择。
tradeoff: Dijkstra（贪心扩展、要求非负权重、更快）vs Bellman-Ford（允许负权、松弛 V-1 轮、更慢）

termDefinitions.meaning: 每一步贪心地扩展当前已知距离最短的未访问节点的最短路算法。

q_en: Why is choosing the shortest task each time not enough for scheduling with dependencies?
options: 任务之间的依赖关系总是可以被贪心直接忽略掉
所有任务其实都必须在同一时刻一起开始
会违反依赖关系，需要先用拓扑排序建立合法顺序，再谈优化
最短任务优先策略在任何依赖场景下都保持最优

All tasks must actually start at the exact same moment.
It can violate dependencies; you need topological sort first to build a valid order, then optimize.

why_en: Dependencies are hard constraints, so topological ordering must come before greedy duration choices.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有依赖、只有独立任务的排序或资源分配，贪心调度可能成立。
tradeoff: 先拓扑排序保证合法顺序（硬约束优先）vs 直接按时长贪心（可能违反依赖）

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每条边都从前面指向后面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so every edge points from earlier to later.

optionExplanations: 忽略依赖会产出违反前置任务顺序的非法调度，依赖是硬约束不是可选项。
有依赖关系恰恰说明某些任务必须等前置任务完成，不是同时开始。
先用拓扑排序拿到不违反依赖的合法顺序，之后才轮到按时长这类软优化。
这个策略只在没有依赖的场景下成立，一旦引入依赖前提就被打破了。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring dependencies produces an illegal schedule that violates ordering -- dependencies are a hard constraint.
Having dependencies means some tasks must wait for others to finish, not that everything starts simultaneously.
Topological sort first gets a legal order that respects dependencies; only then does duration optimizing make sense.
This strategy only holds with no dependencies -- once dependencies exist, its premise breaks.

q: 哪些情况说明贪心可能不是精确正确的答案？
q_en: Which situations suggest greedy may not be an exact correct answer?
options: 选择组合之间相互影响，早期选择会锁死后续
题目要求精确最大价值的 0/1 knapsack
硬币面额是任意集合而不是已知规范系统
区间调度要求最大数量且按结束时间选择
options_en: Choices interact with each other, so an early choice can lock out later possibilities.
The problem requires the exact maximum value for 0/1 knapsack.
The coin denominations are an arbitrary set, not a known canonical system.
Interval scheduling asks for the maximum count and picks greedily by end time.
why: 前三项都有反例风险或需要全局状态。标准最大不重叠区间是贪心可证明正确的例外。
why_en: Greedy is suspect when choices interact, exact knapsack is required, or arbitrary coin systems can create counterexamples.
tradeoff: 存在反例风险的场景（DP/回溯更安全）vs 可证明精确的标准贪心（区间调度）
optionExplanations: 早期选择锁死后续可能性，正是贪心选择性质被破坏的典型信号。
0/1 knapsack 通常需要 DP，按密度贪心可能拿到远低于最优的价值。
非规范面额下最大硬币贪心有已知反例，不能默认它总是对的。
这恰恰是贪心可证明精确正确的经典场景，不属于'贪心可能不精确'这一类。
optionExplanations_en: An early choice locking out later options is the textbook sign the greedy-choice property has broken down.
0/1 knapsack usually needs DP; greedy by value density can land far below the true optimum.
Arbitrary denominations have known counterexamples for largest-coin greedy -- it can't be assumed to always work.
This is exactly the case where greedy is provably exact, so it doesn't belong in the 'may not be exact' bucket.

scenario: AI 刚生成一个贪心方案，你还没证明它正确。
scenario_en: The AI has just generated a greedy solution, and you have not proven it correct yet.
q: AI 刚生成一个贪心方案、还没证明它正确时，最有价值的下一句提示是什么？
q_en: When the AI has generated a greedy solution but you have not proven it correct, what is the most useful next prompt?
options: 请把所有变量名改得更短一些
不用测试，直接提交这个方案
把代码里的注释全部删掉
请给我一个能让这个贪心策略失败的小输入
options_en: Shorten every variable name in the code.
Skip testing and submit this solution directly.
Delete all the comments from the code.
Give me a small input where this greedy strategy could fail.
why: AI 很擅长写贪心，也擅长找反例。让它生成 adversarial tests 能把隐含正确性假设暴露出来。
why_en: Asking the AI for a small failing input turns a greedy assumption into something testable.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经能给出清楚交换论证，仍应补几个边界测试，但不一定需要长时间找反例。
tradeoff: 先要反例验证（多花几分钟、降低盲信风险）vs 直接信任提交（快但可能踩坑）
optionExplanations: 变量名长短跟算法是否正确毫无关系，这不是有价值的下一句。
跳过测试直接提交正是要避免的风险行为，一旦策略有问题会直接带进生产。
注释多少不影响这段贪心是否安全，删注释解决不了正确性问题。
让 AI 主动构造失败输入，能把'贪心可能错'这个隐含假设变成可测试的具体反例。
optionExplanations_en: Variable-name length has nothing to do with whether the algorithm is correct -- not a useful next prompt.
Skipping tests and submitting right away is exactly the risk to avoid -- a bad strategy goes straight to production.
Comment count doesn't affect whether the greedy logic is safe -- deleting comments doesn't touch correctness.
Asking the AI to construct a failing input turns 'greedy might be wrong' into a concrete, testable case.

scenario: 题目是 NP-hard 装箱变体，面试官没有要求精确最优，只要实用分配。
scenario_en: The problem is an NP-hard packing variant, and the interviewer wants a practical assignment rather than an exact optimum.
q: 面对 NP-hard 装箱变体，提示 AI 时应该明确说清什么？
q_en: For an NP-hard packing variant, what should you make explicit when prompting the AI?
options: 用贪心启发式，并说明已知的近似保证或明确不保证最优
直接声称这个方案一定能返回最优解
完全不用向 AI 说明任何取舍问题
让 AI 忽略容量检查以简化实现代码
options_en: Ask for a greedy heuristic and state the known approximation bound or that optimality isn't guaranteed.
Claim outright that the solution is definitely guaranteed to be optimal.
Don't bother explaining any tradeoff to the AI at all.
Have the AI skip capacity checks entirely to simplify the code.
why: NP-hard 场景下，正确表述“启发式/近似”比假装精确更重要。面试官会看你是否理解保证范围。
why_en: For NP-hard packing variants, prompt for a heuristic and explicitly state whether it is approximate rather than optimal.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确要求精确最优且规模小，应转向搜索、DP 或整数规划式建模。
tradeoff: 启发式+明确近似保证（诚实、可用）vs 声称精确最优（误导、风险高）
optionExplanations: 把'启发式还是精确'这条边界讲清楚，是 NP-hard 场景下最重要的一句提示。
对 NP-hard 问题做这种精确性承诺本身就站不住，一被追问就露馅。
不说明取舍会让 AI 和面试官都误判这段代码的保证范围。
跳过容量检查会产出物品总量超出箱子容量的不合法分配。
optionExplanations_en: Spelling out the heuristic-vs-exact boundary is the single most important thing to state for an NP-hard case.
Promising exact optimality for an NP-hard problem doesn't hold up -- it falls apart under any follow-up question.
Leaving the tradeoff unstated lets both the AI and the interviewer misjudge what this code actually guarantees.
Skipping the capacity check can produce an illegal assignment where the total exceeds bin capacity.

q: 验证一段贪心代码时，第一件事应该先说清楚什么？
q_en: When verifying greedy code, what should you state first?
options: 这段代码一共写了多少行
这段代码每一步的贪心选择到底是什么
变量命名是否足够优雅
代码是否用了最新的语言特性
options_en: How many lines of code it has in total.
Exactly what local choice this greedy code commits to at each step.
Whether the variable names are elegant.
Whether it uses the newest language features.
why: 如果说不清“每步选择什么”，就无法证明或反驳它。贪心 bug 多数在策略，不在实现。
why_en: Greedy verification starts by naming the exact local choice the algorithm commits to.
optionExplanations: 行数多少跟策略是否正确没有关系，不是审查该先看的东西。
说不清每一步到底选了什么，后面的交换论证或反例都无从谈起。
命名风格可以随时重构，不影响这次要验证的正确性问题。
语言新特性跟局部选择是否安全无关，不是审查的切入点。
optionExplanations_en: Line count has nothing to do with whether the strategy is correct -- not where a review should start.
Without pinning down exactly what gets chosen at each step, there's no exchange argument or counterexample to build.
Naming style can be refactored anytime and doesn't touch the correctness question being reviewed.
Newer language features say nothing about whether the local choice is safe -- not the right entry point.

q: 审查 AI 生成的贪心解时，应按哪些维度检查？
q_en: When reviewing an AI-generated greedy solution, which dimensions should you check?
options: 贪心选择具体是什么
贪心选择性质是否成立、能否找到反例
是否跑过 adversarial（对抗性）测试用例
NP-hard 问题是否被错误地声称为精确最优
options_en: What exactly the greedy choice is.
Whether the greedy-choice property holds, or a counterexample exists.
Whether adversarial test cases were run.
Whether an NP-hard problem is wrongly claimed to be exactly optimal.
why: 贪心实现通常短，真正风险是策略不正确或保证说错。测试要专门针对策略弱点。
why_en: Greedy review focuses on the choice, its proof or counterexample, adversarial tests, and whether optimality claims are valid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门设计用来暴露算法弱点的刁钻测试输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An adversarial test case is a tricky input specifically designed to expose an algorithm's weakness.

optionExplanations: 先说清选择规则，后续每一步检查才有抓手，挡住连规则都没说清就验证的空转。
直接检查局部最优会不会伤害全局最优，反例一旦找到就直接证伪，挡住盲信。
用刁钻输入主动暴露隐藏 bug，挡住只测 happy path 留下的死角。
确认保证范围没被夸大，挡住把 NP-hard 近似算法误说成精确解的风险。
optionExplanations_en: Naming the exact rule first gives every later check something to grab onto -- blocks reviewing before it's even stated.
Checking whether local optimality holds catches an unsafe choice the moment a counterexample turns up, blocking blind trust.
Tricky inputs surface hidden bugs -- this blocks the blind spot a happy-path-only test would leave.
Confirming the stated guarantee isn't inflated blocks the risk of calling an NP-hard heuristic an exact solution.

scenario: AI 为任意硬币找零写了“每次取不超过剩余金额的最大硬币”。
scenario_en: The AI wrote largest coin not exceeding the remaining amount for arbitrary coin change.
q: 下面哪组测试输入最能暴露这个策略不总是最优？
q_en: Which test input best exposes that this strategy is not always optimal?
codeSample:
while amount > 0:
    coin = max(c for c in coins if c <= amount)
    amount -= coin
    used.append(coin)
options: coins=[1,5,10,25], amount=30
coins=[1], amount=3
coins=[1,3,4], amount=6
coins=[1,2], amount=4
options_en: coins = [1, 5, 10, 25], amount = 30
coins = [1], amount = 3
coins = [1, 3, 4], amount = 6
coins = [1, 2], amount = 4
why: 这个输入下贪心用 4+1+1 三枚，最优是 3+3 两枚。它直接证明任意面额不能用最大硬币贪心当精确解。
why_en: The 1,3,4 coin counterexample exposes that largest-coin greedy is not exact for arbitrary denominations.
whenOtherWins: 在某些规范面额系统里最大硬币策略确实成立，但不能把这个性质推广到任意面额。
tradeoff: 非标准面额（贪心可能出错，需要反例验证）vs 标准/规范面额（贪心通常成立）
optionExplanations: 美分式标准面额下贪心恰好最优，暴露不出问题。
只有一种面额，没有'选哪个'的分支可比较，谈不上反例。
这组面额让贪心多花一枚硬币（4+1+1 对 3+3），是教科书级的反例。
这组小面额下贪心和最优解本来就一致，同样暴露不出问题。
optionExplanations_en: Standard denominations like these make greedy exactly optimal -- nothing to expose here.
With only one denomination there's no branch to compare, so there's no counterexample to find.
This set makes greedy spend one coin too many, 4+1+1 versus 3+3 -- a textbook counterexample.
Greedy and optimal already agree on this small set, so it exposes nothing either.

q: 把贪心题的 AI 面试工作流按顺序排列。
q_en: Put the AI interview workflow for greedy problems in order.
steps: 提示 AI 实现具体策略，并说明 exact 还是 heuristic。
识别优化目标和自然排序键。
寻找小反例或给出交换论证。
明确每一步的贪心选择。
用 adversarial tests 验证策略和边界。
why: 贪心不能先写代码再补理由：先说清选择、验证它，再让 AI 实现，最后用反例式测试守住正确性。
why_en: A solid greedy workflow names the ordering and choice, proves or refutes it, then implements and adversarially tests it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Name[Name greedy choice] --> Test[Try counterexample]
  Test --> Proof[Explain why safe]
  Proof --> Code[Ask AI to code]
  Code --> Adversarial[Run adversarial tests]

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门设计用来暴露算法弱点的刁钻测试输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adversarial tests are tricky inputs specifically designed to expose an algorithm's weakness.

q: 贪心题里，直觉版 exchange argument 要表达什么？
q_en: In a greedy problem, what should an intuitive exchange argument show?
options: 所有局部选择天然就是正确的、无需验证
只要提前排序了就不需要再额外证明什么
找反例远比写测试用例更没有意义
任意最优解都可以把某一步换成贪心选择、结果不会变差
options_en: Every local choice is naturally correct by default, no verification needed.
Sorting alone already means you no longer need to prove anything further.
Hunting for counterexamples is far less useful than writing test cases.
Any optimal solution can have one step swapped for the greedy choice without getting worse.
why: 不需要形式化证明，但要能说明为什么把最优解的某一步换成贪心选择不会损失。区间按结束时间就是典型例子。
why_en: An exchange argument shows that an optimal solution can include the greedy choice without getting worse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 交换论证：证明把最优解中的某一步换成贪心选择不会使结果变差的推理方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An exchange argument shows that swapping in the greedy choice cannot make an optimal solution worse.

optionExplanations: 这正是需要被验证、而不能默认成立的假设，盲信它是贪心题最容易踩的坑。
很多排序正确但选择规则错误的方案照样能通过'排过序'这一步，排序不能替代论证。
反例恰恰是最快的证伪手段，往往比跑一整套测试用例更快定位问题。
这是交换论证的标准表述：把最优解的某一步换成贪心选择，结果不会更差。
optionExplanations_en: That's exactly the assumption that needs verifying, not assumed -- trusting it blindly is the easiest greedy trap.
Plenty of solutions sort correctly but pick the wrong rule and still pass the 'it's sorted' check.
A counterexample is often the fastest way to disprove an idea, faster than running a full test suite.
This is the standard exchange argument: swap one step of an optimal solution for the greedy choice and it won't get worse.

scenario: 你无法在两分钟内给出严谨贪心证明，但也没找到反例。
scenario_en: You cannot give a rigorous greedy proof within two minutes, but you have not found a counterexample either.
q: 两分钟内给不出严谨证明、也没找到反例时，面试中务实的下一步是什么？
q_en: If you cannot prove greedy rigorously within two minutes and have not found a counterexample, what is the practical interview next step?
options: 说贪心看似合理，让 AI 生成对抗测试，失败转 DP/回溯
假装已经完成了严谨的正确性证明和推导
把已经写好的所有测试用例全部删掉
只跑一次简单的 happy path 就算测试完成
options_en: Say greedy looks reasonable, ask the AI for adversarial tests, and be ready to pivot to DP or backtracking.
Pretend a rigorous correctness proof and derivation already exist.
Delete every test case that has already been written.
Run one simple happy-path case and call testing fully done.
why: 找反例不是形式证明，但能降低盲信风险。透明地说出验证计划比沉默提交更好。
why_en: If proof is uncertain, adversarial tests and a clear fallback keep the greedy choice honest.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目是已知经典贪心，如最大不重叠区间，可以更快给出交换论证并实现。
tradeoff: 透明地说出验证计划、留退路（诚实、可核查）vs 沉默直接提交（快但不可信）
optionExplanations: 把不确定性说出来、用对抗测试兜底，是没时间做严谨证明时最诚实也最可核查的做法。
假装证明存在是面试里最危险的行为之一，一被追问细节就会露馅。
删掉已有测试不会让一个不确定的贪心方案变得更可信，只会降低可核查性。
只跑一条 happy path 无法暴露贪心选择性质是否成立，验证强度不够。
optionExplanations_en: Saying greedy looks reasonable and backing it with adversarial tests is the most honest, checkable move here.
Pretending a proof exists is one of the riskiest things to do in an interview -- it falls apart under follow-up.
Deleting existing tests doesn't make an uncertain greedy solution more trustworthy, only less checkable.
A single happy-path run can't expose whether the greedy-choice property actually holds -- not enough verification.

q: 填空：对待 AI 的贪心输出。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: how to treat an AI-generated greedy output.
text: AI 生成的贪心方案应先视为{{假设}}，再用{{证明或反例}}验证，而不是直接当答案。
why: AI 会对很多不适合贪心的问题也给出贪心代码。你的判断力体现在能不能质疑并验证这个策略。
why_en: Treat an AI-generated greedy solution as a hypothesis until proof or counterexamples support it.

q: 下面哪些现实场景本质上是 bin packing 问题？
q_en: Which real-world scenarios are essentially bin-packing problems?
options: 把任务分配到内存容量固定的服务器上
把货物装进容量固定的箱子里运输
把文件放进大小固定的磁盘分区
把课程按先修依赖关系排出学习顺序
options_en: Assigning tasks to servers with fixed memory capacity.
Loading goods into fixed-capacity shipping boxes.
Placing files onto fixed-size disk partitions.
Ordering courses by their prerequisite dependencies.
why: 前三个都是“所有物品放进尽量少的固定容量容器”。课程依赖排序是拓扑排序，不是装箱。
why_en: Server allocation, container packing, and disk partition placement are common bin-packing framings.
optionExplanations: 任务=物品、内存上限=箱子容量，可以直接套 FFD 等装箱贪心。
货物装箱是装箱问题最直观的现实原型，容量约束完全对应。
文件=物品、分区容量=箱子容量，本质上也是同一种容量装箱问题。
课程排序关心先后顺序合不合法，不是容量装不装得下，属于拓扑排序而非装箱。
optionExplanations_en: Tasks map to items and memory cap maps to bin capacity -- FFD-style bin-packing heuristics apply directly.
Loading cargo is the most intuitive real-world bin-packing scenario, with capacity mapping straight across.
Files map to items and partition size maps to bin capacity -- the same capacity-packing structure underneath.
Course ordering is about whether a sequence is legal, not whether things fit -- that's topological sort, not packing.

q: AI 注释说“FFD 返回最优装箱数”，你应该怎样处理？
q_en: If an AI comment says FFD returns the optimal bin count, how should you handle it?
options: 保留这句注释，因为 AI 写的注释一定是正确的
纠正为启发式/近似算法，除非有额外证明或规模允许精确搜索
直接删掉容量限制来简化这个问题
改成用 DFS 但完全不检查任何约束
options_en: Keep the comment, because AI-written comments are always correct.
Correct it to say heuristic or approximate, unless there's extra proof or the size allows an exact search.
Simply delete the capacity constraint to simplify this problem.
Switch to using DFS but skip checking any constraints entirely.
why: 装箱精确最优是 NP-hard，FFD 通常不是最优保证。错误的保证陈述本身就是面试风险。
why_en: FFD should be framed as a heuristic or approximation, not as an exact optimal bin-packing algorithm.
tradeoff: 如实标注为启发式/近似（诚实但听起来'不够强'）vs 声称精确最优（听起来自信但可能是错误陈述）

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把物品按大小从大到小排序，再依次执行 First-Fit 装箱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest-first, then applies First-Fit bin packing.

optionExplanations: AI 生成的注释和代码一样需要核实，'AI 写的一定对'本身就是要打破的假设。
多项式时间内很难对装箱给出精确解，FFD 只是有界近似，纠正成启发式才符合事实。
删约束会让问题变得和原来的业务问题不再等价，是在回避而不是解决。
不检查约束的 DFS 会产出超出容量的非法分配，丢了装箱问题最基本的前提。
optionExplanations_en: AI-written comments need verification just like AI-written code -- 'AI wrote it so it's correct' is the assumption to break.
There's no known polynomial-time exact solver for packing, and FFD is only a bounded approximation, so 'heuristic' matches the facts.
Deleting the constraint makes the problem no longer equivalent to the original one -- that's dodging it, not solving it.
DFS without constraint checks can produce an assignment that exceeds capacity, dropping the packing problem's basic premise.

scenario: 你要计算至少需要多少服务器处理一批有开始/结束时间的任务。
scenario_en: You need to compute the minimum number of servers required for tasks with start and end times.
q: 本质上，这个“最少服务器数”问题要追踪的是什么量？
q_en: At its core, what quantity does this minimum-server problem need to track?
options: 耗时最长的那个任务的名字
开始时间最早的那一个任务
任意时刻同时活跃的任务的最大重叠数
图里随便一条不含环的路径
options_en: The name of the single longest-running task.
The single task with the earliest start time.
The maximum number of simultaneously active tasks at any moment.
Any acyclic path in the graph.
why: 每个同时活跃的区间都需要一个资源。最大重叠数就是最少资源数，最小堆做的是在线追踪活跃结束时间。
why_en: Minimum resources for intervals is the maximum number of simultaneously active intervals.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务没有时间区间而是固定容量装箱，问题转向 bin packing。
tradeoff: 统计任意时刻最大重叠数（决定最少资源数）vs 选出最多不重叠子集（决定最多能选几个）
optionExplanations: 名字是标签不是数值，决定不了需要多少台服务器。
只看一个任务的开始时间，忽略了'同时有几个任务在跑'这个关键信息。
同时活跃的任务各需要一台服务器，峰值重叠数直接等于最少服务器数。
这题没有图和路径的概念，是区间重叠问题，路径无关。
optionExplanations_en: A name is a label, not a number -- it can't determine how many servers are needed.
Looking at one task's start time ignores how many tasks are running at the same moment.
Each simultaneously active task needs its own server, so the peak overlap count is the minimum server count.
There's no graph or path concept here -- this is an interval-overlap problem, unrelated to paths.

q: 贪心题里，哪些表现是强信号？
q_en: In greedy problems, which behaviors are strong interview signals?
options: 能说明为什么局部选择在全局上是安全的，哪怕只是直觉版交换论证
能区分'贪心是近似'和'贪心是错误'这两种不同情况
贪心不成立时，能准确指出该换 DP、回溯还是拓扑排序
无条件相信 AI 给出的第一个贪心方案
options_en: Can explain why the local choice is globally safe, even with just an intuitive exchange argument.
Can tell apart 'greedy is approximate' from 'greedy is wrong'.
When greedy fails, can correctly name DP, backtracking, or topological sort as the fix.
Trusts the AI's first greedy solution unconditionally.
why: 面试官看的是判断力：何时用、为何对、错了怎么换。盲信 AI 贪心输出正是风险点。
why_en: Strong greedy answers justify the local choice, separate approximation from wrongness, and name the right fallback.
optionExplanations: 哪怕只是直觉版交换论证，也挡住了'选了就选了、不问为什么安全'这种空谈。
分清'非最优但有保证'和'不满足题意'，挡住把该换算法的场景误判成可以接受。
错了能立刻点名 DP/回溯/拓扑排序，挡住卡在原地继续硬调贪心的风险。
无条件信任第一版方案，正是要避免的弱信号，容易把错误方案直接带进代码。
optionExplanations_en: Even just an intuitive exchange argument blocks the empty claim of 'I picked it, trust me' with no reasoning.
Telling apart 'non-optimal but guaranteed' from 'fails the requirement' blocks mistaking a must-switch case as fine.
Naming DP, backtracking, or topological sort the moment greedy fails blocks getting stuck endlessly tweaking it.
Trusting the first draft unconditionally is exactly the weak signal to avoid -- it can carry a bug into the code.

q: 把面试中处理 bin packing 的思路按顺序排列。
q_en: Put the interview approach for bin packing in order.
steps: 说明这是 NP-hard 风格问题，精确最优不一定是目标。
实现后要求 AI 生成小型基准和边界容量测试。
先把业务问题翻译成物品、箱子和容量。
选择 FFD 等贪心启发式，并明确不是保证精确最优。
若输入规模或要求需要，再讨论有序结构或搜索优化。
why: 先翻译问题、说清保证范围，再选贪心启发式并测试；优化数据结构是后续步骤，不能先于正确框架。
why_en: A bin-packing interview answer translates the domain, states hardness, chooses a heuristic, tests it, and only then optimizes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Model[Recognize packing] --> Guarantee[State heuristic scope]
  Guarantee --> FFD[Use FFD baseline]
  FFD --> Tests[Test adversarial order]
  Tests --> Optimize[Optimize data structure if needed]

q: 贪心题在 AI Coding 面试中的核心考点是什么？
q_en: What is the core interview skill for greedy problems in AI coding interviews?
options: 只让 AI 写出尽量短小的代码
把所有优化问题都强行套上贪心
只讨论时间复杂度而不讨论正确性
判断贪心是否适用，说清保证并验证 AI 输出
options_en: Just have the AI write the shortest possible code.
Force every optimization problem into a greedy shape.
Only discuss time complexity and skip correctness.
Judge whether greedy applies, state its guarantee, and verify the AI's output.
why: 贪心代码通常不难，难的是策略判断。强候选人会把 AI 生成的贪心当作需要验证的工程假设。
why_en: Greedy interview performance is about judgment: when it applies, what it guarantees, and how you verify it.
optionExplanations: 代码长短跟策略是否正确没有关系，不是这类题的考察重点。
很多问题（比如 0/1 knapsack）贪心并不精确，强行套用会踩坑。
复杂度好看但答案是错的，仍然是一个错误答案，正确性不能被跳过。
判断适用性、讲清保证范围、验证 AI 输出，三件事合起来才是真正的分水岭。
optionExplanations_en: Code length has nothing to do with whether the strategy is correct -- not what this type of problem tests.
Plenty of problems, like 0/1 knapsack, aren't solved exactly by greedy -- forcing it there just creates bugs.
A nice-looking complexity with a wrong answer is still a wrong answer -- correctness can't be skipped.
Judging fit, stating the guarantee clearly, and verifying the AI's output together separate strong answers from weak ones.
